name: Thoracic extension over a roller
summary: A roller across the upper back; hands behind the head, arch backward over it.
setup: Lie with a foam roller across the upper back, knees bent, hands supporting the head. Let the upper back arch over the roller, then come back up. Move the roller a few centimetres and repeat.
why: The arch is small and the head and arms hide the shoulder line from the side. Logged by hand.
regression: Smaller arch; a rolled towel instead of a roller.
contraindications: Osteoporosis, or pain in the lower back during the arch.

faults.label: Arching from the lower back
faults.tip: The roller sits under the ribs, not the lower back. Arching low is where people get sore.

faults.label: Arching the lower back instead
faults.tip: Keep the buttocks on the floor and the stomach lightly braced so the arch stays in the upper back.

faults.label: Pulling on the neck
faults.tip: Cradle the head; the neck should feel no strain.

faults.label: Working only one spot
faults.cue: Move the roller up a level
faults.tip: Do a few arches, then shift the roller a hand-width and repeat.

guide.surface: Firm floor with the roller across the shoulder blades.
guide.stop: Lower back pain, or tingling in the arms.
guide.cannotSee: The arch — the head and arms are in the way.

points.t: Arches over the roller, one segment at a time.
